description:
FOUND s438 (Opus 5), by the very first two-file run of the #472 PCL_DROP_LOG
instrument -- which is the argument for that instrument: this drop is in a file
NO census population reads (perl-tests/t/test.pl is not perl-tests/*.t), and it
is re-transpiled by every one of the 108 sweep files.

THE COMPILER GAP, minimised:

  my $ok = 1; my $f;
  my $so = $ok ? <$f> // "" : "";      # PCL: statement dropped
                                       #      "Bug. Fell through. Missing case: ["

  Neighbours that DO lower:
    $ok ? <$f> : ""                    ok      (no //)
    $ok ? readline($f) // "" : ""      ok      (readline instead of <$f>)
    <$f> // ""                         ok      (no ternary)

  So it is the `<...>` readline token in a ternary BRANCH followed by `//`.
  Same family as docs/ppi-glob-disambiguation.md / the readline-vs-glob
  boundary; the term walker is where it fails.

WHERE IT BITES: perl-tests/t/test.pl lines 179-180, inside runperl_and_capture:

    my $so = do { local $/; open(my $f, '<', $out) ? <$f> // '' : '' };
    my $se = do { local $/; open(my $f, '<', $err) ? <$f> // '' : '' };

Both statements are dropped, in EVERY sweep file's run.  Post-flip they DIE
when reached.  Today the cost is zero because no perl-tests file calls
runperl_and_capture (it exists for t/run/runenv.t's try()), but it is a
landmine under the companion population.

AND THE HARNESS LINE IS WRONG IN REAL PERL TOO -- fix that in the same commit,
not by copying it: `my $f` declared in the ternary's CONDITION is not in scope
in the ternary's own branches, so `<$f>` reads the (unopened) package handle
and `// ''` turns the undef into "".  Probed against perl 5.40: the function
returns ('','') for a file that plainly contains "hello\n".  The correct
spelling is the one two lines below it in the same file:

    my $so = do { local $/; open(my $f, '<', $out) or die; <$f> };   # gives "hello\n"

BAR: the compiler fix gets a Pl/t row for the minimised shape plus the three
neighbours above (they must keep lowering).  The test.pl repair is a HARNESS
change -- the WHAT-TO-RUN table's harness row: full sweep AND `--all --quick`,
both populations, baselines edited row by row.  The two changes may ride
together but the harness half must be measured on its own.

HARNESS HALF DONE s440 (Fable, alone, as ruled): perl-tests/t/test.pl runperl_and_capture now reads the two files perl's-own-t/test.pl way (`if (open(my $f, ...)) { $so = <$f> // '' }` under one `local $/`) -- the `my $f` in a ternary CONDITION was never in scope in its branches (a `my` takes effect at the NEXT statement; probed: the old line returned "" for a file holding "hello\n" in real perl).  Measured ALONE on the s440 merged tree: sweep TOTAL 18313 (+0), GATE clean, drops 5 = census, CHILD DROPS 241 in 98 files -> 9 in 6 files (the remaining nine: six one-off child programs + core Devel/Peek.pm:59, #483).  The companion runner uses this file as its STUB (shadow t/), so its `--all --quick` is owed and runs with the s440 batch legs.  REMAINING (Opus filler): the COMPILER half -- `$ok ? <$f> // "" : ""` drops (a readline token in a ternary branch followed by //); Pl/t row for the minimised shape + the three neighbours.
COMPILER HALF DONE s446k (Opus, agent K of round 5).  #479 CLOSED (both halves).

ROOT CAUSE, and it is NOT a term-walker gap: it is docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md
Â§14 with a CASCADE (now Â§14b).  Â§14 -- a term-position `<$f>` lexed as
`Operator(<) Symbol($f) Operator(>)` -- has been covered since s404 by
Pl::PExpr::_fix_ppi_glob_after_block rebuilding the QuoteLike::Readline token.
What that cannot reach: once `>` is an operator, the tokenizer is in
operator-just-seen state, so the NEXT `/` starts a MATCH.

    $ok ? <$f> // "" : ""   ->  â¦ Operator(>) Regexp::Match(//) Quote::Double("")
    $ok ? <$f> / 2 : ""     ->  â¦ Operator(>) Regexp::Match(/ 2 : "";)   <- the REST

By the time PExpr rebuilds `<$f>` the `//` is a Regexp token where an operator
belongs (hence "Missing case: [...Readline...,Regexp::Match<//>,...]"), and in
the `/ 2` spelling the rest of the statement is inside one token, so no
token-level repair can undo it.

FIX: Pl::Parser2::_repair_readline_cascade -- a SOURCE-level rewrite +
reparse (the _rewrite_state_prepass pattern).  `<$f>` becomes `readline($f)`,
which perlop says is the same thing and which PCL already lowers identically
(probed: scalar and list context, a bareword handle, an undef handle with //,
a false ternary branch that must not read).  `readline(...)` and NOT `(<$f>)`
because parenthesising creates perl's `print (â¦) interpreted as function`
gotcha for `print <$f> // ""`.

CONDITION (narrow by construction, so nothing PPI got right is disturbed):
the `<` must be in TERM position (_ends_term says no), the body must be
perlop's readline body (a simple scalar, possibly qualified, or a bareword
handle -- `<>` is left alone: ARGV magic, and PExpr's rebuild skips it too),
and the token after the `>` must be the Regexp the mis-lex created.

MEASURED: the cascade occurs in ZERO sites of all four in-repo populations
(1329 files scanned; 74 readline-shaped `<` runs are mis-lexed and repaired by
the existing PExpr workaround, none of them followed by a `/`).  So
Pl/t/readline-ternary-01.t (12 rows, inverse-run) IS the guard -- corpus-diff,
the sweep and the companion cannot see this shape at all.

RESIDUE FILED: #563 -- the same cascade with a glob PATTERN body
(`sort <./nope-*-xyz>`, `sort <op/*.t>`) is NOT repaired, because the body is
not a readline body and by then it is inside the Regexp token's text.
subject: PCL cannot lower `COND ? <$fh> // "" : ""` -- a readline followed by // inside a ternary branch; it is the FIRST thing the #472 child-drop instrument found, and it sits in perl-tests/t/test.pl, our own harness (whose runperl_and_capture is ALSO wrong in real perl)
